diagnostics.message: The webhook Lambda is created with a dynamic `vpc_config` (subnets/security groups), but nothing orders `aws_lambda_function.webhook` after `aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.webhook_vpc_execution_role`. Lambda validates that the execution role can call `ec2:CreateNetworkInterface` at function creation, so when `lambda_subnet_ids` is set the function can fail with "The provided execution role does not have permissions to call CreateNetworkInterface on EC2". Add `depends_on = [aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.webhook_vpc_execution_role]` to the function (no attribute reference can express this).

`aws_lambda_function.scale_up` gets a `vpc_config` while `aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.scale_up_vpc_execution_role` (AWSLambdaVPCAccessExecutionRole) is applied in parallel — the function only references the role itself, not the attachment. When `lambda_subnet_ids` is non-empty, function creation can fail because the role cannot create ENIs yet. Add an explicit `depends_on` on the attachment; there is no attribute to reference.

`aws_lambda_function.scale_down` is created with a `vpc_config` but does not depend on `aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.scale_down_vpc_execution_role`; the only link is through `aws_iam_role.scale_down.arn`. With `lambda_subnet_ids` configured the VPC execution role must be attached before the function is created, otherwise the apply fails on ENI permissions. Use an explicit `depends_on`.

The syncer Lambda has a `vpc_config` but no dependency on `aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.syncer_vpc_execution_role` (it only references `aws_iam_role.syncer_lambda.arn`). The AWSLambdaVPCAccessExecutionRole attachment must exist before the function to satisfy Lambda's ENI permission check when VPC subnets are supplied. Add `depends_on` on the attachment; no data reference can express this.

`aws_lambda_function.pool` is created with a `vpc_config` in parallel with `aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.pool_vpc_execution_role`, and Terraform sees no edge between them. The VPC execution role attachment must be applied first (Lambda validates ENI permissions at CreateFunction), so add an explicit `depends_on`; there is no attribute reference to wire in.

`aws_sqs_queue_policy.build_queue_dlq_policy` is meant to attach the deny-insecure-transport policy to the dead-letter queue, but it sets `queue_url = aws_sqs_queue.queued_builds.id`, so it never references `aws_sqs_queue.queued_builds_dlq`. As a result it has no ordering dependency on the DLQ (the policy can be applied before/after the DLQ arbitrarily) and it silently manages the same queue policy as `build_queue_policy`, which the other resource overwrites. Point `queue_url` at the DLQ instead.
